short: Three British Mark IVs met three German A7Vs at Villers-Bretonneux on 24 April 1918.
full:
In fog on the morning of 24 April 1918 the Germans attacked Villers-Bretonneux, the last high ground before Amiens, with infantry and thirteen A7Vs. Near Cachy three of them ran into a section of three Mark IVs under Lieutenant Frank Mitchell of A Company, 1st Battalion, Tank Corps. The two female Mark IVs had only machine guns; the A7V Nixe, commanded by Leutnant Wilhelm Biltz, holed both with its 57 mm gun and they pulled back. Mitchell's male tank, firing its 6-pounder while moving over rough ground with half his crew gassed, hit Nixe three times. It heeled into a shell hole and the crew baled out.

The other two A7Vs withdrew under fire. Seven Whippets then caught German infantry in the open and scattered them, losing four of their number to artillery, and Mitchell's tank was finally disabled by a mortar round. Australian brigades retook the town that night. The engagement lasted minutes and settled nothing, but every armoured force afterwards had to plan for tanks meeting tanks.
